claims.quote: The voice of another aerocab driver hailing them made them realize that there were still ties that bound them to Earth, and they moved apart a little self-consciously, as a cab drew alongside their own.
claims.description: Personal flying taxis (aerocabs) serve as ordinary city transport.

claims.quote: Ralph had immediately transmitted the lost girl's photograph to the Central Office where it was placed before a Telephot connecting with every member of the entire police force, and the picture was reproduced for them in their portable radio instruments for ten seconds
claims.description: Photographs are transmitted by radio to every police officer's portable device, which displays the image.

claims.quote: he sprang to the nearest Telephot. And within fifteen minutes every detective and special agent had been notified
claims.description: A videophone-like device (Telephot) allows instant long-distance audio-visual communication.

claims.quote: with strict orders to record every message, to tune into everything, and to take the messages down on the recorder discs.
claims.description: Radio messages are automatically recorded onto discs for later playback.

claims.quote: A pulsating polarized ether wave, if directed on a metal object can be reflected in the same manner as a light-ray is reflected from a bright surface or from a mirror.
claims.description: Radar-like system that bounces polarized waves off a spacecraft, identifies its metal by reflection factor, and computes its distance from echo time.

claims.quote: it was not until the year 2659 that […] succeeded in accurately determining the exact location of flyers, in space, beyond the reach of the most powerful telescope.
claims.description: Spacecraft can be tracked accurately beyond telescope range.

claims.quote: Overboard went the glass doors, cushions, matting, even the hood of the machine.
claims.description: Private licensed space flyers capable of travel to other planets are bought commercially from manufacturers.

claims.quote: As all space flyers must be licensed by law, he had no trouble in getting the information he desired.
claims.description: Space flyers are legally registered and licensed, with a registry police can query.

claims.quote: The manufacturer also told him that the entire outside shell was of Magnelium—an invention of Ralph's—and that this flyer was the first to be equipped with the new metal.
claims.description: A new metal alloy, Magnelium, is used for spacecraft hulls.

claims.quote: Dismay seized the scientist, as, breaking the seal of the wrapper, he read the printed words:
claims.description: A unified Earth government headed by a 'Planet Governor' with numbered-name citizens and laws forbidding scientists to endanger their lives.

claims.quote: Allow me furthermore to point out to you that under the law "+" scientists are not allowed to endanger their lives under any circumstances.
claims.description: Law forbids scientists from endangering their lives, treating them as protected assets.

claims.quote: I pricked his hand with a little Catalepsol. In fifteen minutes he will be all right again.
claims.description: A drug that induces temporary rigid paralysis on skin contact, wearing off in fifteen minutes.

claims.quote: Towards the end of the twenty-first century, when atmospheric flying had become common, scientists began seriously to think of constructing machinery to enable man to leave the confines of the planet
claims.description: Atmospheric flight becomes common by the late 21st century, prompting serious efforts toward space travel.

claims.quote: the enormous population of Earth, which had passed the twelve billion mark, clamored for an adequate outlet which the planet itself could no longer furnish.
claims.description: Earth's population exceeds twelve billion, creating acute economic pressure and demand for space expansion.

claims.quote: it was equally well known that Earth's scientists and engineers felt that they could, in a few years' time, make it habitable.
claims.description: The airless, sterile Moon could be made habitable (terraformed) by engineers within a few years.

claims.quote: the Anti-Gravitator was invented by the American 969L 9 in the year 2210.
claims.description: A gyroscope-based anti-gravity device is invented that overcomes Earth's gravity, enabling space flight.

claims.quote: it became possible to lift a weight of 1,000 kilograms with an anti-gravitator weighing but 12 kilograms.
claims.description: Anti-gravitators lift 1,000 kg while weighing only 12 kg.

claims.quote: Ralph had struck him senseless with his Radioperforer.
claims.description: A radio-based directed-energy weapon that knocks out a person through a spacecraft window.

claims.quote: A new machine of a well-known Detroit firm had been registered four days ago
claims.description: Detroit continues as a manufacturer, now of space flyers.

claims.quote: Thus a man weighing eighty kilograms on a spring scale on the earth, would weigh but thirty kilograms on the planet Mars. On the sun, however, he would weigh 2232 kilograms.
claims.description: Weight varies with the gravity of different celestial bodies (an accurate prediction of Martian and solar surface weights).

claims.quote: in the exact center of the flyer, all objects lost their weight entirely.
claims.description: Objects at the center of a spacecraft are weightless and float freely.

claims.quote: Sleep was practically impossible. There being nothing to tire the occupant, sleep is unnecessary.
claims.description: In space, with no physical exertion, a traveler cannot sleep and does not need to.

claims.quote: The air supply was manufactured by chemical means on board, but very little was needed, as the original supply taken from the earth is used over and over by altering the carbonic acid gas by means of automatic generators.
claims.description: Closed-loop spacecraft life support that regenerates air by chemically processing carbon dioxide.

claims.quote: the space flyer would become a tiny planet, and as such was subject to the universal laws of the planetary system.
claims.description: A spacecraft stopped at the gravitational neutral point between two bodies would orbit the sun like a tiny planet.

claims.quote: Ralph's machine had made 80,000 miles an hour since its start.
claims.description: Spacecraft travel at tens of thousands of miles per hour, reaching Mars in about thirty days.

claims.quote: He pushed the connecting tube of his flyer into the tube-joint of Fernand's machine. With great care he made the joint air-tight.
claims.description: Two spacecraft can dock in flight via an airtight connecting tube, letting people cross between them.

claims.quote: Surely, not to Venus where the inhabitants were nearly all Terrestrials, and whose laws were identical with those of Earth.
claims.description: Venus is colonized by Earth people under Earth-identical laws.

claims.quote: He knew enough of the Martian character to realize that Alice was in the hands of a man who, once the die was cast, would stop at nothing.
claims.description: Mars is inhabited by an intelligent humanoid race, seven feet tall with enormous eyes, with their own sects and marriage customs.

claims.quote: There remained only the Asteroids.
claims.description: Asteroids can serve as hideaway habitats where people can live.

claims.quote: Ralph applied a small electrical shocking device to the spine of the insensible man, with the result that in a few minutes Fernand opened his eyes
claims.description: An electrical device applied to the spine can revive an unconscious person.
